title: Koszul generators from a conormal fibre basis
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ a prime ideal, and $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ an ideal generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Put $A_{\mathfrak p}=(A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}A$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let $I_{\mathfrak p}=IA_{\mathfrak p}$. Let $r\geq0$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in I$ have images forming a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-basis of $I_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pI_{\mathfrak p}$. There exists $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that the images of $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in $A_s=A[1/s]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] generate $IA_s$ and form a Koszul-regular sequence in $A_s$. Empty sequences are allowed, and $A$ need not be Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 067N (lemma-generate-regular-ideal), assertion (3), applied to the ideal sheaf associated to I on Spec(A), and restricted to a principal open neighbourhood of the specified prime.

proof.text: Choose a finite Koszul-regular tuple $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ generating $I$, as the hypothesis permits. Set $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $J=IR$, and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pR$. The localization map $A\to R$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], so [lem-sc-koszul-regular-flat-base-change] makes the image tuple $g$ Koszul-regular over $R$. It generates $J$: a fraction with numerator in $I$ is a linear combination of the images of the $g_j$. Consequently [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis] gives the specified $R/J$-basis $[g_j]$ of $J/J^2$.

source.place: Tag 067N (lemma-generate-regular-ideal), proof, first paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tags 062H and 062I.

proof.text: Because $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, we have $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and $J^2\subseteq\mathfrak mJ$. In the basis just obtained, the submodule $\mathfrak m(J/J^2)=\mathfrak mJ/J^2$ corresponds exactly to $(\mathfrak m/J)^{\oplus m}$: multiplying arbitrary coordinate vectors by elements of $\mathfrak m$ gives precisely these coordinate vectors. Quotienting the basis isomorphism therefore gives $(R/\mathfrak m)^{\oplus m}\simeq J/\mathfrak mJ$, sending the standard vectors to the images of the $g_j$. Thus those images are a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-basis. Together with the assumed basis of images of the $f_i$, equality of the finite dimensions gives $m=r$.

source.place: Tag 067N (lemma-generate-regular-ideal), proof, first paragraph: equality of the number of generators; explicit quotient-coordinate verification using Tag 062I.

proof.text: After identifying the two tuple lengths, choose $c_{ij}\in A$ with $f_i=\sum_{j=1}^r c_{ij}g_j$, since $f_i\in I=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$. Let $C=(c_{ij})$ and $s=\det C$. On $J/\mathfrak mJ$ the reduction $\overline C$ is the change matrix between the two bases, hence is invertible. Taking determinants shows that the image of $s$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is nonzero. Therefore $s\notin\mathfrak p$: an element of $\mathfrak p$ maps to $\mathfrak pR$ and then to zero in that residue field.

source.place: Tag 067N (lemma-generate-regular-ideal), proof, first paragraph: write the coefficient matrix and invert its determinant.

proof.text: Work in $A_s$ as defined in [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The image of $s$ is a unit, so the adjugate identity gives the inverse matrix $C^{-1}=s^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(C)$. The identities $f=Cg$ and $g=C^{-1}f$ show that the two tuples generate the same ideal of $A_s$, namely $IA_s$. These are actual identities over $A_s$, not only identities in the stalk at $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 067N (lemma-generate-regular-ideal), proof, first paragraph: shrinking to the invertible-matrix locus.

proof.text: The map $A\to A_s$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Applying [lem-sc-koszul-regular-flat-base-change] to the original Koszul-regular tuple $g$ makes its image in $A_s$ Koszul-regular. Both image tuples have length $r$ and generate $IA_s$ by the preceding step, so [lem-sfb-koszul-equal-length-generators] applies over $A_s$ and proves Koszul-regularity of the image tuple $f$. This establishes both required conclusions with the single element $s\notin\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 067N (lemma-generate-regular-ideal), final paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), assertion (3).

proof.text: If $r=0$, the fibre-basis calculation forces $m=0$; the original empty tuple therefore generates $I=0$. The empty matrix has determinant $1$, so the construction gives $s=1$ and the empty Koszul-regular tuple over $A$. A prime is proper, hence the residue field used for equality of dimensions is nonzero. The zero ring has no prime and gives no additional case. No step assumes that $A$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 067N (lemma-generate-regular-ideal), assertion (3): empty-tuple and arbitrary-ring cases of the matrix argument.

proof_origin.place: Tag 067N (lemma-generate-regular-ideal), proof of (3): conormal fibre rank and invertible coefficient matrix; final regularity supplied by more-algebra.tex Tag 066A(3).
